Under current law, the Attorney General can appoint an interim U.S. Attorney for up to 120 days.

If the position remains vacant, district court judges can step in and appoint their own pick to serve indefinitely.

No judge should be able to bypass the Senate, sideline the President, and install their own pick with no time limit.

We introduced the No Appointments by Rogue Judges Act to close this loophole permanently.

Judges interpret the law. They do not get to decide who enforces it.
